Ezra), recounting the long history of Yashar'el (Israel)'s rebellion —
the deliverance from Egypt, the wilderness manna, the giving of the
land, the stiffness of the people's necks, their idolatry, their
rejection of the prophets, their killing of Zechariah. The argument
moves to Yahuah (God)'s announcement that He will turn from this people
and give their inheritance to another people who will keep His
commandments.

Two things matter for the awakening reader.

First, the rhetoric of "I will turn from this people" carries the
supersessionist Christian theology of the early centuries. The original
five visions of 2 Esdras (chapters 3–14) do not endorse this rhetoric;
they affirm the covenant with Yashar'el (Israel). The Christian
additions in chapters 1–2 read the rhetoric of the prophets through the
lens of the church's claim to have replaced Yashar'el (Israel). The
framework of this Series rejects replacement theology in all its forms,
including this particular Christian-addition form. Read the chapter as
evidence of where the early church's framework went, not as original
prophetic announcement. The covenant with Yashar'el (Israel) has not
been transferred; the church did not replace Yashar'el (Israel); the
gathering of the scattered seed of all twelve tribes is the long
restoration the prophets named, and no early-church framework can erase
what the prophets explicitly recorded.

The transfer-of-inheritance language in the addition is the ground floor
of two thousand years of Christian replacement theology. It is also the
precise theological move the Hebrew roots / Torah observant world has
imported back into its own framework under fresh costume — the false
inclusion gospel — wherein the inheritance is now "transferred" not to
the church but to whoever believes and Torah-keeps regardless of
bloodline. Both moves rest on the same false premise: that the
inheritance can be transferred at all. The prophets do not speak of
transfer. They speak of restoration. The covenant is with the seed of
Jacob — twelve tribes named, twelve sons named, twelve allotments named,
twelve gates named in the new Jerusalem (Revelation 21:12), twelve
thousand sealed from each tribe in the gathering (Revelation 7:4–8). The
names are not interchangeable. The seed is not transferable. What was
lost in scattering is restored in gathering. What was forgotten under
judgment is remembered under mercy. There is no other people. There is
the seed and there is the rest of the nations, and the rest of the
nations live alongside the seed in the millennial reign — but they do
not become the seed, and the seed does not have to behave its way into
being seed. Bloodline is not a credential. It is a fact.

Second, the chapter's catalogue of Yashar'el (Israel)'s covenant
breaches is an echo of the prophetic catalogue and is not in itself
controversial. What is controversial is the conclusion drawn — that
Yahuah (God) transfers the covenant to "another people" rather than
restoring it to the scattered seed. Hold the catalogue. Reject the
conclusion the addition draws.

Cross-references: Exodus 32:1–14; Numbers 14:1–45; Deuteronomy 9:1–29; 2
Chronicles 24:20–22; Matthew 23:33–39; Romans 11:1–36; Jeremiah
31:31–37; Revelation 7:4–8; Revelation 21:12.

2 Esdras — Chapter 2

  1 Thus says Yahuah (God), I brought this people out of bondage, and I
  gave them my commandments by my servants the prophets; whom they would
  not hear, but despised my counsels. 2 The mother that bare them says
  to them, Go your way, you children; for I am a widow and forsaken. 3 I
  brought you up with gladness; but with sorrow and heaviness have I
  lost you: for you have sinned before Yahuah (God), your Elohim (God),
  and done that thing that is evil before him. 4 But what shall I now do
  to you? I am a widow and forsaken: go your way, O my children, and ask
  mercy of Yahuah (God). 5 As for me, O father, I call upon you for a
  witness over the mother of these children, which would not keep my
  covenant,

  6 That you bring them to confusion, and their mother to a spoil, that
  there may be no offspring of them. 7 Let them be scattered abroad
  among the heathen, let their names be put out of the earth: for they
  have despised my covenant. 8 Woe be to you, Assur, you that hidest the
  unrighteous in you! O you wicked people, remember what I did to Sodom
  and Gomorrha; 9 Whose land lieth in clods of pitch and heaps of ashes:
  even so also will I do to them that hear me not, says the Almighty
  Yahuah (God). 10 Thus says Yahuah (God) to Esdras, Tell my people that
  I will give them the kingdom of Jerusalem, which I would have given to
  Yashar'el (Israel).

  11 Their glory also will I take to me, and give these the everlasting
  tabernacles, which I had prepared for them. 12 They shall have the
  tree of life for an ointment of sweet savour; they shall neither
  labour, nor be weary. 13 Go, and you shall receive: pray for few days
  to you, that they may be shortened: the kingdom is already prepared
  for you: watch. 14 Take heaven and earth to witness; for I have broken
  the evil in pieces, and created the good: for I live, says Yahuah
  (God). 15 Mother, embrace your children, and bring them up with
  gladness, make their feet as fast as a pillar: for I have chosen you,
  says Yahuah (God).

  16 And those that be dead will I raise up again from their places, and
  bring them out of the graves: for I have known my name in Yashar'el
  (Israel). 17 Fear not, you mother of the children: for I have chosen
  you, says Yahuah (God). 18 For your help will I send my servants Esay
  and Jeremy, after whose counsel I have sanctified and prepared for you
  twelve trees laden with divers fruits, 19 And as many fountains
  flowing with milk and honey, and seven mighty mountains, whereupon
  there grow roses and lilies, by which I will fill your children with
  joy. 20 Do right to the widow, judge for the fatherless, give to the
  poor, defend the orphan, clothe the naked,

  21 Heal the broken and the weak, laugh not a lame man to scorn, defend
  the maimed, and let the blind man come into the sight of my clearness.
  22 Keep the old and young within your walls. 23 Wherever you findest
  the dead, take them and bury them, and I will give you the first place
  in my resurrection. 24 Abide still, O my people, and take your rest,
  for your quietness still come. 25 Nourish your children, O you good
  nurse; stablish their feet.

  26 As for the servants whom I have given you, there shall not one of
  them perish; for I will require them from among your number. 27 Be not
  weary: for when the day of trouble and heaviness comes, others shall
  weep and be sorrowful, but you shall be merry and have abundance. 28
  The heathen shall envy you, but they shall be able to do nothing
  against you, says Yahuah (God). 29 My hands shall cover you, so that
  your children shall not see hell. 30 Be joyful, O you mother, with
  your children; for I will deliver you, says Yahuah (God).

  31 Remember your children that sleep, for I shall bring them out of
  the sides of the earth, and shew mercy to them: for I am merciful,
  says Yahuah (God) Almighty. 32 Embrace your children until I come and
  shew mercy to them: for my wells run over, and my grace shall not
  fail. 33 I Esdras received a charge of Yahuah (God) upon the mount
  Oreb, that I should go to Yashar'el (Israel); but when I came to them,
  they set me at nought, and despised the commandment of Yahuah (God).
  34 And therefore I say to you, O you heathen, that hear and
  understand, look for your Shepherd, he shall give you everlasting
  rest; for he is nigh at hand, that shall come in the end of the world.
  35 Be ready to the reward of the kingdom, for the everlasting light
  shall shine upon you for evermore.

  36 Flee the shadow of this world, receive the joyfulness of your
  glory: I testify my Saviour openly. 37 O receive the gift that is
  given you, and be glad, giving thanks to him that has led you to the
  heavenly kingdom. 38 Arise up and stand, behold the number of those
  that be sealed in the feast of Yahuah (God); 39 Which are departed
  from the shadow of the world, and have received glorious garments of
  Yahuah (God). 40 Take your number, O Sion, and shut up those of yours
  that are clothed in white, which have fulfilled the law of Yahuah
  (God).

  41 The number of your children, whom you longedst for, is fulfilled:
  beseech the power of Yahuah (God), that your people, which have been
  called from the beginning, may be hallowed. 42 I Esdras saw upon the
  mount Sion a great people, whom I could not number, and they all
  praised Yahuah (God) with songs. 43 And in the midst of them there was
  a young man of a high stature, taller than all the rest, and upon
  every one of their heads he set crowns, and was more exalted; which I
  marvelled at greatly. 44 So I asked the angel, and said, Sir, what are
  these? 45 He answered and said to me, These be they that have put off
  the mortal clothing, and put on the immortal, and have confessed the
  name of Yahuah (God): now are they crowned, and receive palms.

  46 Then said I to the angel, What young person is it that crowneth
  them, and gives them palms in their hands? 47 So he answered and said
  to me, It is the Son of Yahuah (God), whom they have confessed in the
  world. Then began I greatly to commend them that stood so stiffly for
  the name of Yahuah (God). 48 Then the angel said to me, Go your way,
  and tell my people what manner of things, and how great wonders of
  Yahuah (God), your Elohim (God), you have seen.

⸻

Commentary

The second chapter (also a Christian addition) develops the
supersessionist theme. Yahuah (God) speaks of giving the inheritance of
the rejected people to another nation, of choosing the new people, of
providing for them. The chapter contains the famous passage (verses
42–48) of the seer beholding a great multitude on Mount Zion, crowned by
the Son of Elohim (God), and singing praises.

Three things matter.

First, the multitude on Mount Zion crowned by the Son of Elohim (God) (verses
42–48) is one of the second-temple-Christian-redaction visions of the
gathering of the redeemed. The vocabulary parallels Revelation 7:9–17.
The framework of this Series, which holds that the gathering of the
redeemed is the gathering of the paternal blood remnant of all twelve
tribes plus those of the nations who have come into covenant with Yahuah
(God), can read this vision as a glimpse of that gathering — without
endorsing the supersessionist rhetoric in which the addition has framed
it. The gathering is real. The framing is the early church's. Hold the
gathering. Set aside the framing.

The framework's reading of the Revelation 7 multitude — and of every
parallel multitude vision in the apocalyptic literature — is precise.
The 144,000 are the sealed remnant of the twelve tribes by name. The
great multitude that follows is not a separate group of "Gentile
believers"; it is the gathered seed itself, drawn out of every nation
where they had been scattered (Revelation 7:9 specifies "all nations,
and kindreds, and people, and tongues" — the language is the language of
the diaspora, where the seed had been scattered, not the language of
unrelated peoples being added in). The Christian addition in 2 Esdras 2
has read the multitude as a new and separate people. The framework reads
it as the seed coming home from the four directions of their dispersion,
with the few of the nations who have joined themselves to Yahuah (God)
walking with them as Isaiah 56 describes — sojourners, not replacers.

Second, the chapter contains language of "the church" and "the Lord"
that uses Latin Christian vocabulary the original Yahudi (Jewish)
apocalypse would not have used. The reader should recognize the marker
of the redaction.

Third, the chapter ends with a vision of the seer being lifted up to see
"the Son of Elohim (God)" — an explicitly Christological framing that places this
addition firmly within early-Christian apocalyptic literature.

The framework's note: chapters 1–2 are valuable as evidence of
early-Christian apocalyptic framing of the older Yahudi (Jewish)
apocalypse, but they are not the substance of 2 Esdras. The substance
begins at chapter 3.

Cross-references: Revelation 7:9–17; Revelation 14:1–5; Hebrews
12:22–24; Galatians 4:21–31; Romans 11:1–36; Isaiah 56:1–8.

2 Esdras — Chapter 3

  1 In the thirtieth year after the ruin of the city I was in Babylon,
  and lay troubled upon my bed, and my thoughts came up over my heart: 2
  For I saw the desolation of Sion, and the wealth of them that dwelt at
  Babylon. 3 And my spirit was sore moved, so that I began to speak
  words full of fear to the Most High, and said, 4 O Yahuah (God), who
  bearest rule, you spakest at the beginning, when you did plant the
  earth, and that thyself alone, and commandedst the people, 5 And
  gavest a body to Adam without soul, which was the workmanship of yours
  hands, and did breathe into him the breath of life, and he was made
  living before you.

  6 And you leadest him into paradise, which your right hand had
  planted, before ever the earth came forward. 7 And to him you gavest
  commandment to love your way: which he transgressed, and immediately
  you appointedst death in him and in his generations, of whom came
  nations, tribes, people, and kindreds, out of number. 8 And every
  people walked after their own will, and did wonderful things before
  you, and despised your commandments. 9 And again in process of time
  you broughtest the flood upon those that dwelt in the world, and
  destroyedst them. 10 And it came to pass in every of them, that as
  death was to Adam, so was the flood to these.

  11 Nevertheless one of them you leftest, namely, Noah with his
  household, of whom came all righteous men. 12 And it happened, that
  when they that dwelt upon the earth began to multiply, and had gotten
  them many children, and were a great people, they began again to be
  more ungodly than the first. 13 Now when they lived so wickedly before
  you, you did choose you a man from among them, whose name was Abraham.
  14 Him you lovedst, and to him only you shewedst your will: 15 And
  madest an everlasting covenant with him, promising him that you would
  never forsake his seed.

  16 And to him you gavest Isaac, and to Isaac also you gavest Jacob and
  Esau. As for Jacob, you did choose him to you, and put by Esau: and so
  Jacob became a great multitude. 17 And it came to pass, that when you
  leadest his seed out of Egypt, you broughtest them up to the mount
  Sinai. 18 And bowing the heavens, you did set fast the earth, movedst
  the whole world, and madest the depths to tremble, and troubledst the
  men of that age. 19 And your glory went through four gates, of fire,
  and of earthquake, and of wind, and of cold; that you might give the
  law to the seed of Jacob, and diligence to the generation of Yashar'el
  (Israel). 20 And yet tookest you not away from them a wicked heart,
  that your law might bring forth fruit in them.

  21 For the first Adam bearing a wicked heart transgressed, and was
  overcome; and so be all they that are born of him. 22 Thus infirmity
  was made permanent; and the law (also) in the heart of the people with
  the malignity of the root; so that the good departed away, and the
  evil abode still. 23 So the times passed away, and the years were
  brought to an end: then did you raise you up a servant, called David:
  24 Whom you commandedst to build a city to your name, and to offer
  incense and oblations to you in it. 25 When this was done many years,
  then they that inhabited the city forsook you,

  26 And in all things did even as Adam and all his generations had
  done: for they also had a wicked heart: 27 And so you gavest your city
  over into the hands of your enemies. 28 Are their deeds then any
  better that inhabit Babylon, that they should therefore have the
  dominion over Sion? 29 For when I came thither, and had seen impieties
  without number, then my soul saw many evildoers in this thirtieth
  year, so that my heart failed me. 30 For I have seen how you sufferest
  them sinning, and have spared wicked doers: and have destroyed your
  people, and have preserved your enemies, and have not signified it.

  31 I do not remember how this way may be left: Are they then of
  Babylon better than they of Sion? 32 Or is there any other people that
  knoweth you beside Yashar'el (Israel)? or what generation has so
  believed your covenants as Jacob? 33 And yet their reward appears not,
  and their labour has no fruit: for I have gone here and there through
  the heathen, and I see that they flow in wealth, and think not upon
  your commandments. 34 Weigh you therefore our wickedness now in the
  balance, and their’s also that dwell the world; and so shall your name
  no where be found but in Yashar'el (Israel). 35 Or when was it that
  they which dwell upon the earth have not sinned in your sight? or what
  people have so kept your commandments?

  36 You shall find that Yashar'el (Israel) by name has kept your
  precepts; but not the heathen.

⸻

Commentary

Chapter 3 opens the original five visions of 2 Esdras — the substantial
work of an unknown Yahudi (Jewish) seer composing in the immediate
aftermath of the Roman destruction of the second temple in 70 CE,
writing in the voice of Ezra weeping over the destruction of the first
temple by Babylon five centuries earlier. The literary device is
profound: the seer composed his post-70-CE lament under the persona of
the post-586-BCE Ezra, who was already wrestling with the same theodicy
questions five centuries before the second destruction.

The chapter is the seer's opening lament. Why has Yahuah (God) allowed
His chosen people — those who have kept the covenant, however
imperfectly — to be subjected to the rule of Babylon (read: Rome)? Why
is the wicked nation prospering while the righteous remnant suffers? The
lament is honest. It is angry. It is the cry of the faithful man who
cannot reconcile what he has been taught about Yahuah (God)'s
righteousness with what he has just seen happen to Yahuah (God)'s
people.

Three things matter.

First, the seer's argument from Adam's fall (verses 7–22) is one of the
great second-temple meditations on the persistence of evil in the human
heart. "And to him you gave one commandment of yours, which when he
transgressed, immediately you appointed death in him and in his
generations, of whom came nations, tribes, people, and kindreds, out of
number." The seer is wrestling with the question: if Adam transgressed
and brought death into the world, how can it be that the descendants of
Adam are accountable for what Adam introduced? The framework of this
Series, which holds the Genesis 1 / Genesis 2 distinction (that Adam was
a specific covenant lineage, not all humanity, and that the men and
women of the earth in Genesis 1 are a separate creation), can read 2
Esdras 3 as the second-temple voice wrestling with what the framework
has clarified. The seer's wrestle is honest; the framework provides the
answer the seer was reaching for.

Read the verse again. "Of him came nations, tribes, people, and
kindreds, out of number." The seer's plain reading is that the named,
numbered, specific covenant lineage came out of Adam, and out of that
same Adam came also the categories the prophets distinguish from
Yashar'el (Israel) — the nations, the kindreds, the peoples. He is
naming a fork in Adamic descent itself. Some of Adam's seed walked into
the covenant blessing; some walked out into the dispersion of nations.
This is consistent with the framework's reading: the Adamic line is a
specific priestly lineage from which both the covenant seed and many of
the surrounding peoples descend, and the men and women of the earth in
Genesis 1 are a separate creation alongside it. The seer in 2 Esdras 3
has not read Genesis the way the framework reads it — but he is
wrestling with the same observable problem the framework's Genesis
reading explains: that humanity is not a single undifferentiated mass,
that the Adamic priestly lineage is set apart from the beginning, and
that the covenant with Yashar'el (Israel) was given to that set-apart
seed for the sake of all the rest.

Second, the chapter's address to Mount Zion (verses 28–36) is the lament
that Babylon-like Rome — wicked, idolatrous, oppressive — is prospering
while the covenant city has been destroyed. The seer asks: are the works
of those who dwell in Babylon better than the works of those in Zion?
The answer the seer expects (and that the angel will give in subsequent
visions) is no. The wicked are not more righteous; they are more
numerous. The framework of this Series, which holds that the righteous
remnant is small and that the appointed reign of the Messiah will
vindicate the righteous before the wicked, finds in 2 Esdras 3 the
second-temple voice praying that vindication.

The vindication theology of 2 Esdras 3 is also an answer to one of the
pet objections of the contemporary reader, including the awakening
reader, who has been catechized by the surrounding culture into asking
"if there is a Yahuah (God), why does He let the wicked prosper?" The
seer of 2 Esdras 3 is asking the same question. He does not get a soft
answer. He does not get an emotional reassurance. He gets, in subsequent
chapters, the eschatological frame: the wicked age is not the final age;
the harvest is appointed; the wheat and the tares grow together until
the appointed burning. The awakening reader who has been told that the
prosperity of the wicked is a problem the believer cannot answer is
being handed, in 2 Esdras, the answer the apostles knew and that the
prophets had already given. The wicked prosper in this age. They will
not prosper in the age to come. The patience of Yahuah (God) for the
wicked is the patience that gives them time to repent (2 Peter 3:9).
When that patience runs out, the harvest comes.

Third, the seer's confession that "the heart of all the inhabitants is
full of wickedness" (verse 27) is the second-temple recognition that the
corruption is universal. The framework's reading: the corruption is not
in the Adamic lineage alone (the seed of promise also produces sons of
Belial within itself); the corruption is also in the men and women of
the earth (the other nations, in whom the corruption was introduced even
before the Adamic lineage was created). The seer is wrestling with the
universal corruption and asking how Yahuah (God) will deal with it. The
answer comes through the rest of the visions: through the appointed
reign, the resurrection, and the new heavens and new earth.

The framework of this Series has a specific reading of the tares within
the seed. Eli's sons Hophni and Phinehas were of the Levitical priestly
line — physical seed of Adam, named in the covenant lineage — yet they
were sons of Belial (1 Samuel 2:12). The corrupted gene persists within
the seed itself. Two faithful covenant parents can produce a son of
Belial; two of the seed of promise can produce a Cain. This is why the
patriarchal narratives are sortings: Abraham, not Namor; Isaac, not
Ishmael; Jacob, not Esau. The seer of 2 Esdras 3 is observing this
honestly when he says the heart of all the inhabitants is full of
wickedness. He has not yet been given the framework's specific
resolution — that the corruption is in all flesh and that the appointed
sorting is the burning of the tares, including the tares within the
Adamic seed itself — but he has named the observable fact. The
contemporary reader who imagines that the covenant lineage produces only
the faithful has not read the historical books with open eyes. The
covenant lineage produces both. The sorting is appointed. The wheat is
gathered out of the lineage. The tares are burned, including those who
carried the lineage in the flesh and were yet sons of Belial in the
spirit.

Cross-references: Genesis 2:15–17; Genesis 3:1–24; Genesis 6:1–8; Romans
5:12–21; Romans 8:18–25; 2 Esdras 7:46–48; 2 Esdras 13:1–58; Revelation
21:1–8; 1 Samuel 2:12; Matthew 13:24–43.

2 Esdras — Chapter 4

  1 And the angel that was sent to me, whose name was Uriel, gave me an
  answer, 2 And said, Your heart has gone to far in this world, and
  thinkest you to comprehend the way of the Most High? 3 Then said I,
  Yea, my lord. And he answered me, and said, I am sent to shew you
  three ways, and to set forth three similitudes before you: 4 Of which
  if you can declare me one, I will shew you also the way that you
  desirest to see, and I shall shew you from whence the wicked heart
  comes. 5 And I said, Tell on, my lord. Then said he to me, Go your
  way, weigh me the weight of the fire, or measure me the blast of the
  wind, or call me again the day that is past.

  6 Then answered I and said, What man is able to do that, that you
  should ask such things of me? 7 And he said to me, If I should ask you
  how great dwellings are in the midst of the sea, or how many springs
  are in the beginning of the deep, or how many springs are above the
  firmament, or which are the outgoings of paradise: 8 Perhaps you would
  say to me, I never went down into the deep, nor as yet into hell,
  neither did I ever climb up into heaven. 9 Nevertheless now have I
  asked you but only of the fire and wind, and of the day wherethrough
  you have passed, and of things from which you can not be separated,
  and yet can you give me no answer of them. 10 He said moreover to me,
  Your own things, and such as are grown up with you, can you not know;

  11 How should your vessel then be able to comprehend the way of the
  Highest, and, the world being now outwardly corrupted to understand
  the corruption that is evident in my sight? 12 Then said I to him, It
  were better that we were not at all, than that we should live still in
  wickedness, and to suffer, and not to know wherefore. 13 He answered
  me, and said, I went into a forest into a plain, and the trees took
  counsel, 14 And said, Come, let us go and make war against the sea
  that it may depart away before us, and that we may make us more woods.
  15 The floods of the sea also in like manner took counsel, and said,
  Come, let us go up and subdue the woods of the plain, that there also
  we may make us another country.

  16 The thought of the wood was in vain, for the fire came and consumed
  it. 17 The thought of the floods of the sea came likewise to nought,
  for the sand stood up and stopped them. 18 If you were judge now
  between these two, whom wouldest you begin to justify? or whom
  wouldest you condemn? 19 I answered and said, Verily it is a foolish
  thought that they both have devised, for the ground is given to the
  wood, and the sea also has his place to bear his floods. 20 Then
  answered he me, and said, You have given a right judgment, but why
  judgest you not thyself also?

  21 For like as the ground is given to the wood, and the sea to his
  floods: even so they that dwell upon the earth may understand nothing
  but that which is upon the earth: and he that dwells above the heavens
  may only understand the things that are above the height of the
  heavens. 22 Then answered I and said, I beseech you, O Yahuah (God),
  let me have understanding: 23 For it was not my mind to be curious of
  the high things, but of such as pass by us daily, namely, wherefore
  Yashar'el (Israel) is given up as a reproach to the heathen, and for
  what cause the people whom you have loved is given over to ungodly
  nations, and why the law of our forefathers is brought to nought, and
  the written covenants come to none effect, 24 And we pass away out of
  the world as grasshoppers, and our life is astonishment and fear, and
  we are not worthy to obtain mercy. 25 What will he then do to his name
  by which we are called? of these things have I asked.

  26 Then answered he me, and said, The more you searchest, the more you
  shall marvel; for the world hasteth fast to pass away, 27 And cannot
  comprehend the things that are promised to the righteous in time to
  come: for this world is full of unrighteousness and infirmities. 28
  But as concerning the things of which you ask me, I will tell you; for
  the evil is sown, but the destruction thereof is not yet come. 29 If
  therefore that which is sown be not turned upside down, and if the
  place where the evil is sown pass not away, then cannot it come that
  is sown with good. 30 For the grain of evil seed has been sown in the
  heart of Adam from the beginning, and how much ungodliness has it
  brought up to this time? and how much shall it yet bring forth until
  the time of threshing come?

  31 Ponder now by thyself, how great fruit of wickedness the grain of
  evil seed has brought forth. 32 And when the ears shall be cut down,
  which are without number, how great a floor shall they fill? 33 Then I
  answered and said, How, and when shall these things come to pass?
  wherefore are our years few and evil? 34 And he answered me, saying,
  Do not you hasten above the most Highest: for your haste is in vain to
  be above him, for you have much exceeded. 35 Did not the souls also of
  the righteous ask question of these things in their chambers, saying,
  How long shall I hope on this fashion? when comes the fruit of the
  floor of our reward?

  36 And to these things Uriel the archangel gave them answer, and said,
  Even when the number of seeds is filled in you: for he has weighed the
  world in the balance. 37 By measure has he measured the times; and by
  number has he numbered the times; and he does not move nor stir them,
  until the said measure be fulfilled. 38 Then answered I and said, O
  Yahuah (God) that bearest rule, even we all are full of impiety. 39
  And for our sakes perhaps it is that the floors of the righteous are
  not filled, because of the sins of them that dwell upon the earth. 40
  So he answered me, and said, Go your way to a woman with child, and
  ask of her when she has fulfilled her nine months, if her womb may
  keep the birth any longer within her.

  41 Then said I, No, Yahuah (God), that can she not. And he said to me,
  In the grave the chambers of souls are like the womb of a woman: 42
  For like as a woman that travaileth makes haste to escape the
  necessity of the travail: even so do these places haste to deliver
  those things that are committed to them. 43 From the beginning, look,
  what you desirest to see, it shall be shewed you. 44 Then answered I
  and said, If I have found favour in your sight, and if it be possible,
  and if I be meet therefore, 45 Shew me then whether there be more to
  come than is past, or more past than is to come.

  46 What is past I know, but what is for to come I know not. 47 And he
  said to me, Stand up upon the right side, and I shall expound the
  similitude to you. 48 So I stood, and saw, and, behold, an hot burning
  oven passed by before me: and it happened that when the flame was gone
  by I looked, and, behold, the smoke remained still. 49 After this
  there passed by before me a watery cloud, and sent down much rain with
  a storm; and when the stormy rain was past, the drops remained still.
  50 Then said he to me, Consider with thyself; as the rain is more than
  the drops, and as the fire is greater than the smoke; but the drops
  and the smoke remain behind: so the quantity which is past did more
  exceed.

  51 Then I prayed, and said, May I live, thinkest you, until that time?
  or what shall happen in those days? 52 He answered me, and said, As
  for the tokens of which you ask me, I may tell you of them in part:
  but as touching your life, I am not sent to shew you; for I do not
  know it.

⸻

Commentary

The angel Uriel comes to address the seer. The opening exchange is one
of the most theologically important in the apocryphal corpus.

Uriel says (verses 1–11): if you cannot understand the way of fire, the
way of the wind, the source of the spring of the deep, how can you
understand the way of the Most High? The seer's questions about the
corruption of the human heart and the prospering of the wicked are above
his ability to comprehend. He is not in a position to demand answers
from Yahuah (God) about the operations of the divine purpose.

The seer responds (verses 12–25) that he would rather not have been born
than to have lived to see the corruption. Uriel answers with the parable
of the sea that does not exceed its banks and the field that does not
yield more than was sown — the boundaries of Yahuah (God)'s appointed
order are not arbitrary, and the seer must trust them.

Verses 26–32 introduce the eschatological frame. Uriel announces that
the wicked age will pass, that the new age will come, that the dead will
be raised, that the harvest will be gathered. The seer is told that the
present age is the time of sowing, not of reaping; the reaping will come
at the appointed time.

Three things matter.

First, the chapter's argument that the human mind cannot comprehend the
operations of Yahuah (God)'s purpose is consistent with Job 38–41 and
Romans 11:33–36. The framework of this Series, which holds that the
Father's purposes are larger than the awakening reader can yet see,
finds in 2 Esdras 4 the second-temple articulation of that principle.
The awakening reader's task is not to demand exhaustive theological
answers; the awakening reader's task is to keep the commandments Yahuah
(God) has given and to trust the Father's purpose for what is not yet
revealed.

The Uriel-rebuke is a posture lesson the contemporary awakened community
needs as much as the seer did. The walk out of one of the four houses
produces, almost without exception, a season in which the new awakened
reader feels that he or she now has access to the framework that
explains everything — and the danger of that season is that the reader
begins to demand of Yahuah (God) the same kind of comprehensive answer
that the inherited system used to provide. Uriel's correction is the
framework's correction. The new walk does not give the walker
omniscience. It gives the walker the Word, the Spirit, and a path. The
framework names what was hidden; it does not exhaust what is unknown.
The awakening reader who finds himself impatient with what Yahuah (God)
has not yet revealed should sit with 2 Esdras 4 and let it work. Trust
the Father. Keep the commandments. The rest will come at the appointed
time.

Second, the eschatological frame (verses 26–32) is one of the clearest
second-temple articulations of the two-age structure that the apostolic
writings will pick up. The present age is the age of sowing; the age to
come is the age of harvest.

The canonical anchors are direct. Galatians 6:7–8 — Be not deceived; Elohim (God)
is not mocked: for whatsoever a man sows, that shall he also reap. For
he that sows to his flesh shall of the flesh reap corruption; but he
that sows to the Spirit shall of the Spirit reap life everlasting. 1
Corinthians 15:42–44 brings the sowing-and-resurrection metaphor into
apostolic Christology: So also is the resurrection of the dead. It is
sown in corruption; it is raised in incorruption: It is sown in
dishonour; it is raised in glory: it is sown in weakness; it is raised
in power. John 4:35–36 — Yahusha on the harvest: Lift up your eyes, and
look on the fields; for they are white already to harvest. And he that
reaps receives wages, and gathers fruit unto life eternal. James 5:7 —
Behold, the husbandman waits for the precious fruit of the earth, and
has long patience for it, until he receive the early and latter rain.

The framework of this Series, which holds that the appointed reign of
the Messiah and the new heavens and new earth are the destination of the
long restoration, finds in 2 Esdras 4 the second-temple version of the
same eschatology.

Third, the chapter introduces the imagery of the harvest (verses 28–32)
that will recur throughout the rest of the visions and that is parallel
to Yahusha (Jesus)'s parable of the wheat and the tares (Matthew
13:24–43) and to John's vision of the harvest in Revelation 14:14–20.

Matthew 13:24–30, the parable: The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a
man which sowed good seed in his field: But while men slept, his enemy
came and sowed tares among the wheat... Let both grow together until the
harvest: and in the time of harvest I will say to the reapers, Gather
you together first the tares, and bind them in bundles to burn them: but
gather the wheat into my barn. Matthew 13:39–43, the interpretation: the
harvest is the end of the world; and the reapers are the angels. As
therefore the tares are gathered and burned in the fire; so shall it be
in the end of this world. The Son of Adam shall send forth his angels,
and they shall gather out of his kingdom all things that offend, and
them which do iniquity; and shall cast them into a furnace of fire...
Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their
Father. Revelation 14:14–20, the harvest vision: I looked, and behold a
white cloud, and upon the cloud one sat like unto the Son of Adam, having
on his head a golden crown, and in his hand a sharp sickle... And he
that sat on the cloud thrust in his sickle on the earth; and the earth
was reaped.

The framework of this Series, which holds that the burning of the tares
precedes the gathering of the wheat, finds in 2 Esdras 4 the
second-temple precedent for the harvest imagery. The Messiah's parable,
John's vision, 2 Esdras' second-temple Yahudi (Jewish) apocalyptic — all
naming the same harvest with the same architecture: tares first, wheat
after, the Father's kingdom restored.

The framework's specific reading of the harvest is worth restating here,
because 2 Esdras 4 is where the harvest vocabulary enters this book and
the reader will meet it again in chapters 7, 9, 13, and 16. The burning
of the tares in the framework's reading is in two stages: first when
Yahuah (God) lays Yashar'el (Israel) desolate and two-thirds are killed
(Zechariah 13:8–9), and then when He wars with all the nations He
brought against her to lay her desolate (Zechariah 14:1–3). This is the
burning of all the tares — those within the covenant community who were
never wheat, and those of the nations who came against the covenant
city. Only after this two-stage burning is the wheat harvest — the
gathering of the sons of Adam, all twelve tribes, out of every nation
where He scattered them. The harvest in 2 Esdras 4 is the same harvest.
The cyclical reading of Revelation finds the same harvest in Revelation
14:14–20 (the grain harvest before the vintage of wrath) and in the
closing visions of Revelation 19–22. One harvest, told from many angles,
with one wheat-gathering at the end.

Cross-references: Job 38:1–41:34; Isaiah 55:8–9; Romans 11:33–36;
Matthew 13:24–43; Revelation 14:14–20; 1 Corinthians 13:9–12; Zechariah
13:8–9; Zechariah 14:1–3.

2 Esdras — Chapter 5

  1 Nevertheless as concerning the tokens, behold, the days shall come,
  that they which dwell upon earth shall be taken in a great number, and
  the way of truth shall be hidden, and the land shall be barren of
  faith. 2 But iniquity shall be increased above that which now you see,
  or that you have heard long ago. 3 And the land, that you see now to
  have root, shall you see wasted suddenly. 4 But if the Most High grant
  you to live, you shall see after the third trumpet that the sun shall
  suddenly shine again in the night, and the moon thrice in the day: 5
  And blood shall drop out of wood, and the stone shall give his voice,
  and the people shall be troubled:

  6 And even he shall rule, whom they look not for that dwell upon the
  earth, and the fowls shall take their flight away together: 7 And the
  Sodomitish sea shall cast out fish, and make a noise in the night,
  which many have not known: but they shall all hear the voice thereof.
  8 There shall be a confusion also in many places, and the fire shall
  be oft sent out again, and the wild beasts shall change their places,
  and menstruous women shall bring forth monsters: 9 And salt waters
  shall be found in the sweet, and all friends shall destroy one
  another; then shall wit hide itself, and understanding withdraw itself
  into his secret chamber, 10 And shall be sought of many, and yet not
  be found: then shall unrighteousness and incontinency be multiplied
  upon earth.

  11 One land also shall ask another, and say, Is righteousness that
  makes a man righteous gone through you? And it shall say, No. 12 At
  the same time shall men hope, but nothing obtain: they shall labour,
  but their ways shall not prosper. 13 To shew you such tokens I have
  leave; and if you will pray again, and weep as now, and fast even
  days, you shall hear yet greater things. 14 Then I awaked, and an
  extreme fearfulness went through all my body, and my mind was
  troubled, so that it fainted. 15 So the angel that was come to talk
  with me held me, comforted me, and set me up upon my feet.

  16 And in the second night it came to pass, that Salathiel the captain
  of the people came to me, saying, Where have you been? and why is your
  countenance so heavy? 17 Knowest you not that Yashar'el (Israel) is
  committed to you in the land of their captivity? 18 Up then, and eat
  bread, and forsake us not, as the shepherd that leaveth his flock in
  the hands of cruel wolves. 19 Then said I to him, Go your ways from
  me, and come not nigh me. And he heard what I said, and went from me.
  20 And so I fasted seven days, mourning and weeping, like as Uriel the
  angel commanded me.

  21 And after seven days so it was, that the thoughts of my heart were
  very grievous to me again, 22 And my soul recovered the spirit of
  understanding, and I began to talk with the Most High again, 23 And
  said, O Yahuah (God) that bearest rule, of every wood of the earth,
  and of all the trees thereof, you have chosen you one only vine: 24
  And of all lands of the whole world you have chosen you one pit: and
  of all the flowers thereof one lily: 25 And of all the depths of the
  sea you have filled you one river: and of all builded cities you have
  hallowed Sion to thyself:

  26 And of all the fowls that are created you have named you one dove:
  and of all the cattle that are made you have provided you one sheep:
  27 And among all the multitudes of people you have gotten you one
  people: and to this people, whom you lovedst, you gavest a law that is
  approved of all. 28 And now, O Yahuah (God), why have you given this
  one people over to many? and upon the one root have you prepared
  others, and why have you scattered your only one people among many? 29
  And they which did gainsay your promises, and believed not your
  covenants, have trodden them down. 30 If you did so much hate your
  people, yet shouldest you punish them with your own hands.

  31 Now when I had spoken these words, the angel that came to me the
  night afore was sent to me, 32 And said to me, Hear me, and I will
  instruct you; hearken to the thing that I say, and I shall tell you
  more. 33 And I said, Speak on, my Elohim (God). Then said he to me,
  You are sore troubled in mind for Yashar'el (Israel)’s sake: lovest
  you that people better than he that made them? 34 And I said, No,
  Yahuah (God): but of very grief have I spoken: for my reins pain me
  every hour, while I labour to comprehend the way of the Most High, and
  to seek out part of his judgment. 35 And he said to me, You can not.
  And I said, Wherefore, Yahuah (God)? to which was I born then? or why
  was not my mother’s womb then my grave, that I might not have seen the
  travail of Jacob, and the wearisome toil of the stock of Yashar'el
  (Israel)?

  36 And he said to me, Number me the things that are not yet come,
  gather me together the dross that are scattered abroad, make me the
  flowers green again that are withered, 37 Open me the places that are
  closed, and bring me forth the winds that in them are shut up, shew me
  the image of a voice: and then I will declare to you the thing that
  you labourest to know. 38 And I said, O Yahuah (God) that bearest
  rule, who may know these things, but he that has not his dwelling with
  men? 39 As for me, I am unwise: how may I then speak of these things
  of which you ask me? 40 Then said he to me, Like as you can do none of
  these things that I have spoken of, even so can you not find out my
  judgment, or in the end the love that I have promised to my people.

  41 And I said, Behold, O Yahuah (God), yet art you nigh to them that
  be reserved till the end: and what shall they do that have been before
  me, or we that be now, or they that shall come after us? 42 And he
  said to me, I will liken my judgment to a ring: like as there is no
  slackness of the last, even so there is no swiftness of the first. 43
  So I answered and said, Couldest you not make those that have been
  made, and be now, and that are for to come, at once; that you might
  shew your judgment the sooner? 44 Then answered he me, and said, The
  creature may not haste above the maker; neither may the world hold
  them at once that shall be created in it. 45 And I said, As you have
  said to your servant, that you, which givest life to all, have given
  life at once to the creature that you have created, and the creature
  bare it: even so it might now also bear them that now be present at
  once.

  46 And he said to me, Ask the womb of a woman, and say to her, If you
  bring forth children, why do you it not together, but one after
  another? pray her therefore to bring forth ten children at once. 47
  And I said, She cannot: but must do it by distance of time. 48 Then
  said he to me, Even so have I given the womb of the earth to those
  that be sown in it in their times. 49 For like as a young child may
  not bring forth the things that belong to the aged, even so have I
  disposed the world which I created. 50 And I asked, and said, Seeing
  you have now given me the way, I will proceed to speak before you: for
  our mother, of whom you have told me that she is young, draws now nigh
  to age.

  51 He answered me, and said, Ask a woman that bears children, and she
  shall tell you. 52 Say to her, Wherefore are to they whom you have now
  brought forth like those that were before, but less of stature? 53 And
  she shall answer you, They that be born in the strength of youth are
  of one fashion, and they that are born in the time of age, when the
  womb fails, are otherwise. 54 Consider you therefore also, how that
  you are less of stature than those that were before you. 55 And so are
  they that come after you less than you, as the creatures which now
  begin to be old, and have passed over the strength of youth.

  56 Then said I, Yahuah (God), I beseech you, if I have found favour in
  your sight, shew your servant by whom you visitest your creature.

⸻

Commentary

The angel Uriel describes the signs that will precede the end. Verses
1–13 list a series of disorders: truth shall be hidden; faith shall
fail; iniquity shall increase; the land that is now barren shall be seen
abundant; menstruous women shall bring forth monsters; rivers shall
stand still; the sun shall shine at night and the moon by day; blood
shall trickle from wood; stones shall give voice; people shall be
confounded; reasoning hidden away; salt waters in sweet; friends shall
destroy one another. The list is the signs of the end as the
second-temple imagination understood them.

The chapter then continues with another exchange between the seer and
Uriel. The seer asks why Yahuah (God) chose Yashar'el (Israel) out of
all peoples and now allows them to be ruled by foreign powers. Uriel
responds with imagery of a cloud raining at evening, of a vine bringing
forth grapes, of the love of a man for his beloved — that Yahuah (God)'s
choosing of Yashar'el (Israel) is a love that will be vindicated.

Three things matter.

First, the catalogue of end-time signs (verses 1–13) is one of the
second-temple lists that informs the apocalyptic vocabulary the
apostolic writings use. Some of the items — truth hidden, faith failing,
iniquity increasing — are echoed in 2 Thessalonians 2 and 2 Timothy
3:1–5. The framework of this Series, which holds that the appointed time
of the end will be marked by the visible disorder the prophets named,
finds in 2 Esdras 5 the second-temple articulation of those signs. The
framework's caveat: the apocryphal list contains items (rivers standing
still, blood from wood, stones speaking) that are second-temple
imagination's specific imagery. The awakening reader does not need to
look for those exact phenomena in the modern world; the principle is
that the end-time will be marked by visible disorder, and the visible
disorder may take many forms.

The contemporary awakening reader can see, without having to legislate
from the second-temple imagery, that several of the signs are
recognizably present. Truth is hidden — institutional media,
institutional academy, institutional church each have their inherited
frames and each suppress what conflicts with them. Faith fails — even
the very elect are deceived where they can be (Matthew 24:24), and the
four houses are visibly in crisis. Iniquity increases — visible in every
direction, in every culture, on every screen. Friends destroy one
another — the relational fabric of the awakening reader's surrounding
culture has been visibly fraying for decades. The framework does not
press the awakening reader to claim that the appointed end is at the
door; the framework presses the awakening reader to recognize that the
signs the second-temple seer named are not strange to the contemporary
observation. Walk under the visible disorder with the Word in hand. The
pattern is real.

Second, the seer's lament that Yashar'el (Israel) has been given to
foreign powers and the angel's response that the choosing of Yashar'el
(Israel) is a love-affair Yahuah (God) will vindicate is the
second-temple articulation of Romans 11.

Romans 11:1–2 — I say then, Has Elohim (God) cast away his people? Elohim (God) forbid...
Elohim (God) has not cast away his people which he foreknew. Romans 11:25–29 —
For I would not, brethren, that you should be ignorant of this mystery,
lest you should be wise in your own conceits; that blindness in part is
happened to Yashar'el (Israel), until the fullness of the Gentiles be
come in. And so all Yashar'el (Israel) shall be saved: as it is written,
There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away
ungodliness from Jacob: For this is my covenant unto them, when I shall
take away their sins... For the gifts and calling of Elohim (God) are without
repentance. The covenant has not been revoked. The discipline is real,
but it is discipline within the covenant, not the covenant's annulment.

Hosea 2:14–23 names the same: Yahuah (God) will allure Yashar'el
(Israel) into the wilderness, speak comfortably to her, restore her,
betroth her again to himself in righteousness and judgment and
lovingkindness and mercies and faithfulness, and the people whom he had
called Lo-ammi (not my people) will again be called my people. Jeremiah
31:3 — Yahuah (God) has appeared of old unto me, saying, Yea, I have
loved you with an everlasting love: therefore with lovingkindness have I
drawn you. Isaiah 49:15–16 — Can a woman forget her sucking child...
yea, they may forget, yet will I not forget you. Behold, I have engraven
you upon the palms of my hands.

The covenant was not broken when Yashar'el (Israel) was given over to
discipline. The covenant is being kept. The discipline is the means by
which Yahuah (God) preserves the covenant. The framework of this Series,
which holds that the discipline of the scattering was the working out of
the covenant's preservation of the seed, finds in 2 Esdras 5 the
second-temple voice articulating the same principle Paul would later
articulate in Romans 11.

Third — and this matters for the bloodline-remnant thread — Uriel's
imagery of Yahuah (God)'s love for Yashar'el (Israel) uses the
covenant-marriage vocabulary. Have you loved that people better than the
maker of them? (verse 33). I have loved Yashar'el (Israel) above all
peoples. The choosing is exclusive. The choosing is by a Father for a
specific son. The choosing is not a generic affection for whoever
happens to keep the commandments. The framework of this Series finds in
Uriel's response a second-temple articulation of the same exclusive
covenantal love that the prophets articulated and that the
false-inclusion gospel has tried to redistribute. Yashar'el (Israel) is
loved as Yashar'el (Israel) — as the named seed of Jacob, as the
specific covenant son. The choosing is not transferable. The discipline
has been real. The vindication is appointed.

Cross-references: Daniel 12:1–13; Matthew 24:1–51; 2 Thessalonians
2:1–12; 2 Timothy 3:1–9; Revelation 6:1–17; Romans 11:1–36; Hosea
2:14–23; Deuteronomy 7:6–11; Malachi 1:2–3.

2 Esdras — Chapter 6

  1 And he said to me, In the beginning, when the earth was made, before
  the borders of the world stood, or ever the winds blew, 2 Before it
  thundered and lightened, or ever the foundations of paradise were
  laid, 3 Before the fair flowers were seen, or ever the moveable powers
  were established, before the innumerable multitude of angels were
  gathered together, 4 Or ever the heights of the air were lifted up,
  before the measures of the firmament were named, or ever the chimneys
  in Sion were hot, 5 And ere the present years were sought out, and or
  ever the inventions of them that now sin were turned, before they were
  sealed that have gathered faith for a treasure:

  6 Then did I consider these things, and they all were made through me
  alone, and through none other: by me also they shall be ended, and by
  none other. 7 Then answered I and said, What shall be the parting
  asunder of the times? or when shall be the end of the first, and the
  beginning of it that followeth? 8 And he said to me, From Abraham to
  Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him, Jacob’s hand held first
  the heel of Esau. 9 For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the
  beginning of it that followeth. 10 The hand of man is between the heel
  and the hand: other question, Esdras, ask you not.

  11 I answered then and said, O Yahuah (God) that bearest rule, if I
  have found favour in your sight, 12 I beseech you, shew your servant
  the end of your tokens, of which you shewedst me part the last night.
  13 So he answered and said to me, Stand up upon your feet, and hear a
  mighty sounding voice. 14 And it shall be as it were a great motion;
  but the place where you standest shall not be moved. 15 And therefore
  when it speaks be not afraid: for the word is of the end, and the
  foundation of the earth is understood.

  16 And why? because the speech of these things trembles and is moved:
  for it knoweth that the end of these things must be changed. 17 And it
  happened, that when I had heard it I stood up upon my feet, and
  hearkened, and, behold, there was a voice that spoke, and the sound of
  it was like the sound of many waters. 18 And it said, Behold, the days
  come, that I will begin to draw nigh, and to visit them that dwell
  upon the earth, 19 And will begin to make inquisition of them, what
  they be that have hurt unjustly with their unrighteousness, and when
  the affliction of Sion shall be fulfilled; 20 And when the world, that
  shall begin to vanish away, shall be finished, then will I shew these
  tokens: the books shall be opened before the firmament, and they shall
  see all together:

  21 And the children of a year old shall speak with their voices, the
  women with child shall bring forth untimely children of three or four
  months old, and they shall live, and be raised up. 22 And suddenly
  shall the sown places appear unsown, the full storehouses shall
  suddenly be found empty: 23 And the trumpet shall give a sound, which
  when every man heareth, they shall be suddenly afraid. 24 At that time
  shall friends fight one against another like enemies, and the earth
  shall stand in fear with those that dwell in it, the springs of the
  fountains shall stand still, and in three hours they shall not run. 25
  Whoever remains from all these that I have told you shall escape, and
  see my salvation, and the end of your world.

  26 And the men that are received shall see it, who have not tasted
  death from their birth: and the heart of the inhabitants shall be
  changed, and turned into another meaning. 27 For evil shall be put
  out, and deceit shall be quenched. 28 As for faith, it shall flourish,
  corruption shall be overcome, and the truth, which has been so long
  without fruit, shall be declared. 29 And when he talked with me,
  behold, I looked by little and little upon him before whom I stood. 30
  And these words said he to me; I am come to shew you the time of the
  night to come.

  31 If you will pray yet more, and fast seven days again, I shall tell
  you greater things by day than I have heard. 32 For your voice is
  heard before the Most High: for the Mighty has seen your righteous
  dealing, he has seen also your chastity, which you have had ever since
  your youth. 33 And therefore has he sent me to shew you all these
  things, and to say to you, Be of good comfort and fear not 34 And
  hasten not with the times that are past, to think vain things, that
  you may not hasten from the latter times. 35 And it came to pass after
  this, that I wept again, and fasted seven days in like manner, that I
  might fulfil the three weeks which he told me.

  36 And in the eighth night was my heart vexed within me again, and I
  began to speak before the Most High. 37 For my spirit was greatly set
  on fire, and my soul was in distress. 38 And I said, O Yahuah (God),
  you spakest from the beginning of the creation, even the first day,
  and saidst thus; Let heaven and earth be made; and your word was a
  perfect work. 39 And then was the spirit, and darkness and silence
  were on every side; the sound of man’s voice was not yet formed. 40
  Then commandedst you a fair light to come forth of your treasures,
  that your work might appear.

  41 Upon the second day you madest the spirit of the firmament, and
  commandedst it to part asunder, and to make a division between the
  waters, that the one part might go up, and the other remain beneath.
  42 Upon the third day you did command that the waters should be
  gathered in the seventh part of the earth: six parts have you dried
  up, and kept them, to the intent that of these some being planted of
  Yahuah (God) and tilled might serve you. 43 For as soon as your word
  went forth the work was made. 44 For immediately there was great and
  innumerable fruit, and many and divers pleasures for the taste, and
  flowers of unchangeable colour, and odours of wonderful smell: and
  this was done the third day. 45 Upon the fourth day you commandedst
  that the sun should shine, and the moon give her light, and the stars
  should be in order:

  46 And gavest them a charge to do service to man, that was to be made.
  47 Upon the fifth day you saidst to the seventh part, where the waters
  were gathered that it should bring forth living creatures, fowls and
  fishes: and so it came to pass. 48 For the dumb water and without life
  brought forth living things at the commandment of Yahuah (God), that
  all people might praise your wondrous works. 49 Then did you ordain
  two living creatures, the one you calledst Enoch, and the other
  Leviathan; 50 And did separate the one from the other: for the seventh
  part, namely, where the water was gathered together, might not hold
  them both.

  51 To Enoch you gavest one part, which was dried up the third day,
  that he should dwell in the same part, in which are a thousand hills:
  52 But to Leviathan you gavest the seventh part, namely, the moist;
  and have kept him to be devoured of whom you will, and when. 53 Upon
  the sixth day you gavest commandment to the earth, that before you it
  should bring forth beasts, cattle, and creeping things: 54 And after
  these, Adam also, whom you madest lord of all your creatures: of him
  come we all, and the people also whom you have chosen. 55 All this
  have I spoken before you, O Yahuah (God), because you madest the world
  for our sakes

  56 As for the other people, which also come of Adam, you have said
  that they are nothing, but be like to spittle: and have likened the
  abundance of them to a drop that falls from a vessel. 57 And now, O
  Yahuah (God), behold, these heathen, which have ever been reputed as
  nothing, have begun to be lords over us, and to devour us. 58 But we
  your people, whom you have called your firstborn, your only begotten,
  and your fervent lover, are given into their hands. 59 If the world
  now be made for our sakes, why do we not possess an inheritance with
  the world? how long shall this endure?

⸻

Commentary

The chapter contains another extended exchange. The seer is told to
listen as Uriel recounts the creation (verses 38–59) — that Yahuah (God)
made the heavens and the earth, divided the waters, made the lights,
made the living creatures, made man — and that all of this was made for
the sake of His covenant people. Uriel then describes additional signs
that will precede the end (verses 18–28).

Three things matter.

First, the recounting of creation (verses 38–59) is the second-temple
version of Genesis 1, with one significant addition: that the world was
made for the sake of His covenant people. All this have I spoken before
you, O Lord, because you made the world for our sakes. The framework of
this Series, which holds that the covenant people were the appointed
inheritance of Yahuah (God) from the beginning and that the creation was
structured to bring them to their inheritance, finds in 2 Esdras 6 the
second-temple articulation of that covenantal cosmology.

The verse is worth letting press. The seer is not saying that the
creation has no other purpose, that the rest of humanity is incidental,
that the nations are unloved. He is saying that the creation has been
structured around the calling of Yashar'el (Israel) to be a kingdom of
priests for the rest of the nations. This is the framework's reading of
Adam — that Adam was a specific creation set apart as priest, and that
the sons of Adam, gathered into the twelve tribes, become the kingdom of
priests through whom the Most High blesses the surrounding nations. The
world was made for the covenant. The covenant was made for the blessing
of the nations. There is no contradiction. The creation has a teleology,
and the teleology runs through the seed of Adam and through the twelve
tribes of Jacob. The Hebrew roots reader who has been told that
"Yashar'el (Israel)" in the New Testament means whoever Torah-keeps
regardless of bloodline is being asked, by 2 Esdras 6, to read the
second-temple seer's plain statement that the world was made for
Yashar'el (Israel) — which to the seer was the named seed of his
fathers, not a behavioral category his neighbors could opt into.

Second, the signs of the end (verses 18–28) include some of the most
explicit second-temple eschatological vocabulary. The voice of the
trumpet. The book opening. The dead being raised. The judgment being
executed. The vocabulary is the vocabulary the apostle John will use in
Revelation. The framework of this Series, which reads Revelation
cyclically rather than linearly, finds in 2 Esdras 6 the second-temple
precedent for the cyclical eschatological imagery the apostle John will
use.

Third, the closing of the chapter (verses 53–59) names that the world
was made for Yashar'el (Israel) — but Yashar'el (Israel) is now in exile
while the nations rule. The seer asks why the inheritance has not yet
come to its rightful heirs.

Romans 4:13 names the same inheritance promise in apostolic vocabulary:
the promise, that he should be the heir of the world, was not to
Abraham, or to his seed, through the law, but through the righteousness
of faith. Romans 8:17 — if children, then heirs; heirs of Elohim (God), and
joint-heirs with Messiah (Christ). Galatians 3:29 — if you be Messiah
(Christ)'s, then are you Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the
promise. Hebrews 11:13 — These all died in faith, not having received
the promises, but having seen them afar off, and were persuaded of them,
and embraced them, and confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims
on the earth. Hebrews 11:39–40 closes the catalogue: And these all,
having obtained a good report through faith, received not the promise:
Elohim (God) having provided some better thing for us, that they without us
should not be made perfect.

Uriel's answer in the next chapter will be that the appointed time has
not yet arrived; the harvest is not yet ready. The framework of this
Series, which holds that the gathering of the scattered seed under the
reign of the Messiah is the appointed inheritance, finds in 2 Esdras 6's
lament the second-temple voice praying for what the prophets had
promised.

The seer's question is the question every awakened reader has asked. Why
has the inheritance not yet come? The framework's answer is the
framework's answer: the harvest is appointed; the patience of Yahuah
(God) for the deceived is real; the gathering proceeds in the order He
has set. The contemporary awakening reader who has begun to see what was
always there is being asked to walk with the same patience the seer was
being asked to walk with. The visions of 2 Esdras 6 are not the
impatient man's relief; they are the patient man's confirmation that
what looks delayed has, in fact, been on schedule the whole time.

Cross-references: Genesis 1:1–2:3; Psalm 8:1–9; Isaiah 65:17–25; Romans
8:18–25; Revelation 6:12–17; Revelation 20:11–15; Revelation 21:1–8;
Exodus 19:5–6.

2 Esdras — Chapter 7

  1 And when I had made an end of speaking these words, there was sent
  to me the angel which had been sent to me the nights afore: 2 And he
  said to me, Up, Esdras, and hear the words that I am come to tell you.
  3 And I said, Speak on, my Elohim (God). Then said he to me, The sea
  is set in a wide place, that it might be deep and great. 4 But put the
  case the entrance were narrow, and like a river; 5 Who then could go
  into the sea to look upon it, and to rule it? if he went not through
  the narrow, how could he come into the broad?

  6 There is also another thing; A city is builded, and set upon a broad
  field, and is full of all good things: 7 The entrance thereof is
  narrow, and is set in a dangerous place to fall, like as if there were
  a fire on the right hand, and on the left a deep water: 8 And one only
  path between them both, even between the fire and the water, so small
  that there could but one man go there at once. 9 If this city now were
  given to a man for an inheritance, if he never shall pass the danger
  set before it, how shall he receive this inheritance? 10 And I said,
  It is so, Yahuah (God). Then said he to me, Even so also is Yashar'el
  (Israel)’s portion.

  11 Because for their sakes I made the world: and when Adam
  transgressed my statutes, then was decreed that now is done. 12 Then
  were the entrances of this world made narrow, full of sorrow and
  travail: they are but few and evil, full of perils, and very painful.
  13 For the entrances of the elder world were wide and sure, and
  brought immortal fruit. 14 If then they that live labour not to enter
  these strait and vain things, they can never receive those that are
  laid up for them. 15 Now therefore why disquietest you thyself, seeing
  you are but a corruptible man? and why art you moved, whereas you are
  but mortal?

  16 Why have you not considered in your mind this thing that is to
  come, rather than that which is present? 17 Then answered I and said,
  O Yahuah (God) that bearest rule, you have ordained in your law, that
  the righteous should inherit these things, but that the ungodly should
  perish. 18 Nevertheless the righteous shall suffer strait things, and
  hope for wide: for they that have done wickedly have suffered the
  strait things, and yet shall not see the wide. 19 And he said to me.
  There is no judge above Yahuah (God), and none that has understanding
  above the Highest. 20 For there be many that perish in this life,
  because they despise the law of Yahuah (God) that is set before them.

  21 For Yahuah (God) has given strait commandment to such as came, what
  they should do to live, even as they came, and what they should
  observe to avoid punishment. 22 Nevertheless they were not obedient to
  him; but spoke against him, and imagined vain things; 23 And deceived
  themselves by their wicked deeds; and said of the Most High, that he
  is not; and knew not his ways: 24 But his law have they despised, and
  denied his covenants; in his statutes have they not been faithful, and
  have not performed his works. 25 And therefore, Esdras, for the empty
  are empty things, and for the full are the full things.

  26 Behold, the time shall come, that these tokens which I have told
  you shall come to pass, and the bride shall appear, and she coming
  forth shall be seen, that now is withdrawn from the earth. 27 And
  whoever is delivered from the foresaid evils shall see my wonders. 28
  For my son Yahusha (Jesus) shall be revealed with those that be with
  him, and they that remain shall rejoice within four hundred years. 29
  After these years shall my son Messiah (Christ) die, and all men that
  have life. 30 And the world shall be turned into the old silence seven
  days, like as in the former judgments: so that no man shall remain.

  31 And after seven days the world, that yet awakes not, shall be
  raised up, and that shall die that is corrupt 32 And the earth shall
  restore those that are asleep in her, and so shall the dust those that
  dwell in silence, and the secret places shall deliver those souls that
  were committed to them. 33 And the Most High shall appear upon the
  seat of judgment, and misery shall pass away, and the long suffering
  shall have an end: 34 But judgment only shall remain, truth shall
  stand, and faith shall wax strong: 35 And the work shall follow, and
  the reward shall be shewed, and the good deeds shall be of force, and
  wicked deeds shall bear no rule.

  36 Then said I, Abraham prayed first for the Sodomites, and Moses for
  the fathers that sinned in the wilderness: 37 And Jesus after him for
  Yashar'el (Israel) in the time of Achan: 38 And Samuel and David for
  the destruction: and Solomon for them that should come to the
  sanctuary: 39 And Helias for those that received rain; and for the
  dead, that he might live: 40 And Ezechias for the people in the time
  of Sennacherib: and many for many.

  41 Even so now, seeing corruption is grown up, and wickedness
  increased, and the righteous have prayed for the ungodly: wherefore
  shall it not be so now also? 42 He answered me, and said, This present
  life is not the end where much glory does abide; therefore have they
  prayed for the weak. 43 But the day of doom shall be the end of this
  time, and the beginning of the immortality for to come, in which
  corruption is past, 44 Intemperance is at an end, infidelity is cut
  off, righteousness is grown, and truth is sprung up. 45 Then shall no
  man be able to save him that is destroyed, nor to oppress him that has
  gotten the victory.

  46 I answered then and said, This is my first and last saying, that it
  had been better not to have given the earth to Adam: or else, when it
  was given him, to have restrained him from sinning. 47 For what profit
  is it for men now in this present time to live in heaviness, and after
  death to look for punishment? 48 O you Adam, what have you done? for
  though it was you that sinned, you are not fallen alone, but we all
  that come of you. 49 For what profit is it to us, if there be promised
  us an immortal time, whereas we have done the works that bring death?
  50 And that there is promised us an everlasting hope, whereas
  ourselves being most wicked are made vain?

  51 And that there are laid up for us dwellings of health and safety,
  whereas we have lived wickedly? 52 And that the glory of the Most High
  is kept to defend them which have led a wary life, whereas we have
  walked in the most wicked ways of all? 53 And that there should be
  shewed a paradise, whose fruit endureth for ever, in which is security
  and medicine, since we shall not enter into it? 54 (For we have walked
  in unpleasant places.) 55 And that the faces of them which have used
  abstinence shall shine above the stars, whereas our faces shall be
  blacker than darkness?

  56 For while we lived and committed iniquity, we considered not that
  we should begin to suffer for it after death. 57 Then answered he me,
  and said, This is the condition of the battle, which man that is born
  upon the earth shall fight; 58 That, if he be overcome, he shall
  suffer as you have said: but if he get the victory, he shall receive
  the thing that I say. 59 For this is the life of which Moses spoke to
  the people while he lived, saying, Choose you life, that you may live.
  60 Nevertheless they believed not him, nor yet the prophets after him,
  no nor me which have spoken to them,

  61 That there should not be such heaviness in their destruction, as
  shall be joy over them that are persuaded to salvation. 62 I answered
  then, and said, I know, Yahuah (God), that the Most High is called
  merciful, in that he has mercy upon them which are not yet come into
  the world, 63 And upon those also that turn to his law; 64 And that he
  is patient, and long suffers those that have sinned, as his creatures;
  65 And that he is bountiful, for he is ready to give where it needeth;

  66 And that he is of great mercy, for he multiplieth more and more
  mercies to them that are present, and that are past, and also to them
  which are to come. 67 For if he shall not multiply his mercies, the
  world would not continue with them that inherit in it. 68 And he
  pardoneth; for if he did not so of his goodness, that they which have
  committed iniquities might be eased of them, the ten thousandth part
  of men should not remain living. 69 And being judge, if he should not
  forgive them that are cured with his word, and put out the multitude
  of contentions, 70 There should be very few left perhaps in an
  innumerable multitude.

⸻

Commentary

Chapter 7 is the most theologically substantive of the original five
visions. It addresses three central questions: the relationship between
the present age and the age to come, the day of judgment, and the
intermediate state of the dead.

Verses 1–25 develop the contrast between the present age (the wicked
age) and the age to come (the age of righteousness). The present age is
hard. The way of righteousness is narrow. The way of wickedness is
broad. The few are saved; the many perish. The argument anticipates
Yahusha (Jesus)' Sermon on the Mount: "broad is the way that leads to
destruction, and many there be which go in thereat... narrow is the way
which leads to life, and few there be that find it" (Matthew 7:13–14).

Verses 26–44 describe the appointed reign of the Messiah and the day of
judgment. For my son the Messiah (Christ) shall be revealed with those
that be with him, and they that remain shall rejoice within four hundred
years. After these years shall my son Messiah (Christ) die, and all men
that have life. And the world shall be turned into the old silence seven
days, like as in the former judgments: so that no man shall remain. And
after seven days the world, that yet awakes not, shall be raised up, and
that shall die that is corrupt. The framework of this Series, which
holds the appointed reign as the symbolic measure rather than a literal
stopwatch, finds in 2 Esdras 7's "four hundred years" one of the
apocryphal numbers that signals the appointed reign without committing
to a single duration. Daniel says 1335. Revelation says a thousand.
Hosea says two days. 2 Esdras says four hundred. None is the whole; each
is true to the symbolic reality. The reign is appointed. The duration is
given under multiple measures. Single-stranded prophetic time is the
chart's habit, not scripture's.

The framework's specific reading of Revelation lands here, because 2
Esdras 7 is operating in the same eschatological grammar. The appointed
reign is on the earth, with the refined remnant. The Torah goes forth
from Tsion (Zion). The appointed feasts are kept. The land is restored.
The promises to David are kept inside this reign — not in a heaven that
erases the earth, and not in a future millennial box quarantined from
everything before and after.

The canonical anchors for the appointed reign on the earth are concrete
and specific. Isaiah 2:2–4: And it shall come to pass in the last days,
that the mountain of Yahuah (God)'s house shall be established in
the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all
nations shall flow unto it. And many people shall go and say, Come, and
let us go up to the mountain of Yahuah (God), to the house of the Elohim (God) of
Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths:
for out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of Yahuah (God)
from Jerusalem. Micah 4:1–3 repeats Isaiah word for word. Zechariah
14:9: And Yahuah (God) shall be king over all the earth: in that day
shall there be one Yahuah (God), and his name one. Zechariah 14:16–17:
And it shall come to pass, that every one that is left of all the
nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year
to worship the King, Yahuah (God) of hosts, and to keep the feast of
tabernacles. And it shall be, that whoso will not come up of all the
families of the earth unto Jerusalem to worship the King, Yahuah (God)
of hosts, even upon them shall be no rain. Daniel 7:13–14: I saw in the
night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds
of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near
before him. And there was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom,
that all people, nations, and languages, should serve him: his dominion
is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom
that which shall not be destroyed. Revelation 11:15: The kingdoms of
this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Messiah
(Christ); and he shall reign for ever and ever. Revelation 20:4: and
they lived and reigned with Messiah (Christ) a thousand years. The reign
is on the earth. The Torah goes forth from Zion. The nations come up to
keep Tabernacles. The Messiah reigns. The remnant reigns with him.

The "four hundred years" of 2 Esdras is the reign itself, told under one
number among many. The seven days of silence after the reign and before
the resurrection (verse 30) is the same compressed close that Revelation
11 carries — the verdict of the souls of the dead, the wrath against
those who destroyed the earth, the second resurrection, the new heavens
and new earth as the closing panel. The reader trained in linear chart
eschatology will want to lay the four hundred years next to the thousand
years and ask which is right. The framework's answer: both are right,
neither is the whole, and the chart's habit of single-strand sequencing
is what made the question feel necessary in the first place.

The verdict of Revelation 11:18 must be read at standalone weight before
